No, not necessarily. "Cage-free" only means the hens are not kept in battery cages. They usually live indoors in barns or aviaries, and common cage-free standards, such as United Egg Producers' Certified Cage-Free, don't require outdoor access. Hens with outdoor access are typically labeled "free-range," and "pasture-raised" usually means more outdoor space.
